fields.title: Pride and Prejudice
fields.description: A classic comedy of manners and romance set in 19th-century England, following the turbulent relationship between Elizabeth Bennet, the daughter of a country gentleman, and Fitzwilliam Darcy, a rich aristocratic landowner.

fields.title: Frankenstein; or, The Modern Prometheus
fields.description: The seminal gothic science-fiction novel telling the story of Victor Frankenstein, a young scientist who creates a sapient creature in an unorthodox scientific experiment, with tragic consequences.

fields.title: The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
fields.description: A collection of twelve short stories featuring the brilliant Victorian consulting detective Sherlock Holmes and his companion Dr. John H. Watson, solving London's most baffling mysteries.

fields.title: Dracula
fields.description: The quintessential epistolary vampire novel detailing Count Dracula's attempt to move from Transylvania to England in search of new blood, and the battle between him and a group of determined adversaries led by Professor Abraham Van Helsing.

fields.title: Alice's Adventures in Wonderland
fields.description: The enchanting story of young Alice falling down a rabbit hole into a subterranean fantasy world populated by peculiar, anthropomorphic creatures.

fields.title: The Great Gatsby
fields.description: Set in the Jazz Age on Long Island, the novel follows narrator Nick Carraway and his interactions with the mysterious millionaire Jay Gatsby and Gatsby's obsession with reunited love Daisy Buchanan.

fields.title: The Time Machine
fields.description: A pioneering science fiction novella about an English scientist and inventor who builds a machine to travel through time, journeying to the year A.D. 802,701 to meet the Eloi and Morlocks.

fields.title: The Metamorphosis
fields.description: The famous novella telling the story of salesman Gregor Samsa, who wakes one morning to find himself inexplicably transformed into a monstrous vermin.

fields.title: A Tale of Two Cities
fields.description: Set in London and Paris before and during the French Revolution, depicting the plight of the French peasantry and the violence of the Reign of Terror.

fields.title: Moby-Dick; or, The Whale
fields.description: The epic narrative of sailor Ishmael and the obsessive quest of Captain Ahab, revenge-driven master of the whaling ship Pequod, seeking the giant white sperm whale Moby Dick.

fields.title: Designing Data-Intensive Applications
fields.description: Data is at the center of many challenges in system design today. Difficult issues need to be figured out, such as scalability, consistency, reliability, efficiency, and maintainability. In this practical and comprehensive guide, author Martin Kleppmann helps you navigate this diverse landscape by examining the pros and cons of various technologies for processing and storing data. Software keeps changing, but the fundamental principles remain the same. With this book, software engineers and architects will learn how to apply those ideas in practice, and how to make full use of data in modern applications. Peer under the hood of the systems you already use, and learn how to use and operate them more effectively.

fields.title: Hands-On Machine Learning with Scikit-Learn, Keras, and TensorFlow
fields.description: Through a series of recent breakthroughs, deep learning has boosted the entire field of machine learning. Now, even programmers who know close to nothing about this technology can use simple, efficient tools to implement programs capable of learning from data. This practical book shows you how. By using concrete examples, minimal theory, and two production-ready Python frameworks—Scikit-Learn and TensorFlow—author Aurélien Géron helps you gain an intuitive understanding of the concepts and tools for building intelligent systems. You’ll learn a range of techniques, starting with simple linear regression and progressing to deep neural networks.

fields.title: Clean Code
fields.description: Even bad code can function. But if code isn’t clean, it can bring a development organization to its knees. Every year, countless hours and significant resources are lost because of poorly written code. But it doesn’t have to be that way. Noted software expert Robert C. Martin presents a revolutionary paradigm with Clean Code: A Handbook of Agile Software Craftsmanship. Martin has teamed up with his colleagues from Object Mentor to distill their best agile practice of cleaning code ‘on the fly’ into a book that will instill within you the values of a software craftsman and make you a better programmer.

fields.title: Deep Learning
fields.description: Deep learning is a form of machine learning that enables computers to learn from experience and understand the world in terms of a hierarchy of concepts. Because the computer gathers knowledge from experience, there is no need for a human computer operator to formally specify all the knowledge that the computer needs. The hierarchy of concepts allows the computer to learn complicated concepts by building them out of simpler ones; a graph of these hierarchies would be many layers deep. This book introduces a broad range of topics in deep learning, covering mathematical and conceptual background, deep learning techniques used in industry, and research perspectives.

fields.title: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach
fields.description: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach offers the most comprehensive, up-to-date introduction to the theory and practice of artificial intelligence. Number one in its field, this textbook is ideal for one or two-semester, undergraduate or graduate-level courses in Artificial Intelligence. The 4th Edition brings readers up to date on the latest technologies, presents concepts in a more unified manner, and offers new or expanded coverage of machine learning, deep learning, transfer learning, multiagent systems, robotics, natural language processing, causality, probabilistic programming, privacy, fairness, and safe AI.

fields.title: The Pragmatic Programmer
fields.description: Straight from the programming trenches, The Pragmatic Programmer cuts through the increasing specialization and technicalities of modern software development to examine the core process—taking a requirement and producing working, maintainable code that delights its users. It covers topics ranging from personal responsibility and career development to architectural techniques for keeping your code flexible and easy to adapt and reuse. Written as a series of self-contained sections and filled with entertaining anecdotes, thoughtful examples, and interesting analogies, The Pragmatic Programmer illustrates the best practices and major pitfalls of many different aspects of software development.

fields.title: Dune
fields.description: Set on the desert planet Arrakis, Dune is the story of the boy Paul Atreides, heir to a noble family tasked with ruling an inhospitable world where the only thing of value is the 'spice' melange, a drug capable of extending life and enhancing consciousness. Coveted across the known universe, melange is a prize worth fighting for. When House Atreides is betrayed, the destruction of Paul's family will set into motion a journey toward a destiny larger than he could ever have imagined.

fields.title: Neuromancer
fields.description: The matrix is a consensus hallucination experienced daily by billions of legitimate operators, in every nation... Case was the sharpest data-thief in the matrix—until he crossed the wrong people and they burned his nervous system with a fungal toxin. Now a charismatic stranger offers him a cure in return for a hack into an unthinkable corporate AI.

fields.title: Foundation
fields.description: For twelve thousand years the Galactic Empire has ruled supreme. Now it is dying. But only Hari Seldon, creator of the revolutionary science of psychohistory, can see into the future—to a dark age of ignorance, barbarism, and warfare that will last thirty thousand years. To preserve knowledge and save humankind, Seldon gathers the best minds of the Empire and brings them to a bleak planet at the edge of the galaxy.

fields.title: The Three-Body Problem
fields.description: Set against the backdrop of China's Cultural Revolution, a secret military project sends signals into space to establish contact with aliens. An alien civilization on the brink of destruction captures the signal and plans to invade Earth. Meanwhile, on Earth, different camps start forming, planning to either welcome the superior beings and help them take over a world seen as corrupt, or to fight against the invasion.

fields.title: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy
fields.description: Seconds before the Earth is demolished to make way for a galactic freeway, Arthur Dent is plucked off the planet by his friend Ford Prefect, a researcher for the revised edition of The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy. Together this dynamic pair begin a journey through space aided by quotes from The Hitchhiker's Guide and a galaxy-full of fellow travelers.

Winston Smith toes the Party line, rewriting history to satisfy the Ministry of Truth. With each lie he writes, Winston grows to hate the Party that seeks power for its own sake and persecutes those who dare to commit thoughtcrimes. But as he starts to think for himself, Winston cannot escape the fact that Big Brother is always watching.

fields.title: To Kill a Mockingbird
fields.description: The unforgettable novel of a childhood in a sleepy Southern town and the crisis of conscience that rocked it. Compassionate, dramatic, and deeply moving, To Kill A Mockingbird takes readers to the roots of human behavior—to innocence and experience, kindness and cruelty, love and hatred, humor and pathos.

fields.title: The Great Gatsby
fields.description: The Great Gatsby, F. Scott Fitzgerald's third book, stands as the supreme achievement of his career. First published in 1925, this quintessential novel of the Jazz Age has been acclaimed by generations of readers. The story of the mysteriously wealthy Jay Gatsby and his unrequited love for the beautiful Daisy Buchanan is an exquisitely crafted tale of America in the 1920s.

fields.title: Brave New World
fields.description: Aldous Huxley's profoundly important classic of world literature, Brave New World is a searching vision of an unequal, technologically-advanced future where humans are genetically bred, socially indoctrinated, and pharmaceutically anesthetized to passively uphold an authoritarian ruling order.

fields.title: One Hundred Years of Solitude
fields.description: The brilliant, bestselling, landmark novel that tells the story of the Buendía family, and chronicles the irreconcilable conflict between the desire for solitude and the need for love—in rich, imaginative magical realism that defined world literature.

fields.title: The Alchemist
fields.description: Paulo Coelho's masterpiece tells the mystical story of Santiago, an Andalusian shepherd boy who yearns to travel in search of a worldly treasure. His quest will lead him to riches far different—and far more satisfying—than he ever imagined.

fields.title: Atomic Habits
fields.description: No matter your goals, Atomic Habits offers a proven framework for improving—every day. James Clear, one of the world's leading experts on habit formation, reveals practical strategies that will teach you exactly how to form good habits, break bad ones, and master the tiny behaviors that lead to remarkable results.

fields.title: Thinking, Fast and Slow
fields.description: In the international bestseller, Thinking, Fast and Slow, Daniel Kahneman, the renowned psychologist and winner of the Nobel Prize in Economics, takes us on a groundbreaking tour of the mind and explains the two systems that drive the way we think. System 1 is fast, intuitive, and emotional; System 2 is slower, more deliberative, and more logical.

fields.title: The Psychology of Money
fields.description: Doing well with money isn’t necessarily about what you know. It’s about how you behave. And behavior is hard to teach, even to really smart people. Money—investing, personal finance, and business decisions—is typically taught as a math-based field, where data and formulas tell us exactly what to do. But in the real world people don’t make financial decisions on a spreadsheet.

fields.title: Zero to One
fields.description: If you want to build a better future, you must believe in secrets. The great secret of our time is that there are still uncharted frontiers to explore and new inventions to create. In Zero to One, legendary entrepreneur and investor Peter Thiel shows how we can find singular ways to create those new things.

fields.title: Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind
fields.description: From a renowned historian comes a groundbreaking narrative of humanity’s creation and evolution—a #1 international bestseller—that explores the ways in which biology and history have defined us and enhanced our understanding of what it means to be human.

fields.title: Deep Work
fields.description: One of the most valuable skills in our economy is becoming increasingly rare. If you master this skill, you'll achieve extraordinary results. Deep work is the ability to focus without distraction on a cognitively demanding task. It's a skill that allows you to quickly master complicated information and produce better results in less time.

fields.title: A Brief History of Time
fields.description: A landmark volume in science writing by one of the great minds of our time, Stephen Hawking’s book explores such profound questions as: How did the universe begin—and what made its start possible? Does time always flow forward? Is the universe unending—or are there boundaries? Are there other dimensions in space? What will happen when it all ends?

fields.title: Cosmos
fields.description: The magnificent story of fifteen billion years of cosmic evolution transforming matter and life into consciousness, of how science and civilization grew up together, and of the forces and individuals that helped shape modern science. A brilliant exploration of universe and humanity.

fields.title: Guns, Germs, and Steel
fields.description: In this 'artful, informative, and delightful' (William H. McNeill, New York Review of Books) book, Jared Diamond convincingly argues that geographical and environmental factors shaped the modern world. Societies that had a head start in food production advanced beyond the hunter-gatherer stage, and then developed religion—as well as nasty germs and potent weapons of war.

fields.title: Meditations
fields.description: A series of personal writings by Marcus Aurelius, Roman Emperor from 161 to 180 AD, recording his private notes to himself and ideas on Stoic philosophy. Marcus Aurelius wrote the 12 books of the Meditations as a source for his own guidance and self-improvement.

fields.title: Python Crash Course
fields.description: Python Crash Course is a fast-paced, thorough introduction to Python that will have you writing programs, solving problems, and making things that work in no time. In the first half of the book, you’ll learn basic programming concepts, such as variables, lists, classes, and loops, and practice writing clean code. In the second half, you’ll put your new knowledge into practice with three projects.

fields.title: Introduction to Algorithms
fields.description: Some books on algorithms are rigorous but incomplete; others cover masses of material but lack rigor. Introduction to Algorithms uniquely combines rigor and comprehensiveness. The book covers a broad range of algorithms in depth, yet makes their design and analysis accessible to all levels of readers. Each chapter is relatively self-contained and can be used as a unit of study.

fields.title: Pride and Prejudice
fields.description: Few have failed to be charmed by the witty and independent Elizabeth Bennet in Austen's beloved classic Pride and Prejudice. When Elizabeth Bennet first meets eligible bachelor Fitzwilliam Darcy, she thinks him arrogant and conceited; he is indifferent to her good looks and lively mind. When she later discovers that Darcy has involved himself in the troubled relationship between his friend Bingley and her beloved sister Jane, she is determined to dislike him more than ever.

fields.title: Structure and Interpretation of Computer Programs
fields.description: Structure and Interpretation of Computer Programs has had a dramatic impact on computer science curricula over the past three decades. This classic book uses the Scheme programming language to explain the fundamental principles of computation, recursion, data abstraction, and interpreter design.

fields.title: Design Patterns: Elements of Reusable Object-Oriented Software
fields.description: Capturing a wealth of experience about the design of object-oriented software, four top-notch designers present a catalog of simple and succinct solutions to commonly occurring design problems. 23 foundational patterns that every software engineer must know.

fields.title: Refactoring: Improving the Design of Existing Code
fields.description: For more than twenty years, serious programmers have relied on Martin Fowler's Refactoring to improve the design of existing code and enhance software maintainability. This completely revised edition shows how to make code simpler, cleaner, and easier to comprehend without changing observable behavior.

fields.title: Cracking the Coding Interview
fields.description: Learn how to uncover the hints and hidden details in questions, discover how to break problems down into manageable chunks, and master algorithm design techniques across arrays, trees, graphs, dynamic programming, and system design.

fields.title: Site Reliability Engineering
fields.description: In this collection of essays and articles, key members of Google's Site Reliability Engineering team explain how and why their commitment to the entire lifecycle has enabled the company to successfully build, deploy, monitor, and maintain some of the largest software systems in the world.

fields.title: Fluent Python
fields.description: Don't waste time trying to bend Python to fit patterns you learned in other languages. Python's simplicity lets you become productive quickly, but this often means you aren't using everything it has to offer. With this updated hands-on guide, you'll learn how to write effective, modern Python 3 code by leveraging its best features.

fields.title: Effective Java
fields.description: The definitive guide to Java platform best practices—updated for Java 7, 8, and 9. Joshua Bloch provides eighty-five best-practice solutions for the programming challenges you encounter every day, from generics and lambdas to streams, serialization, and concurrency.

fields.title: Grokking Algorithms
fields.description: Grokking Algorithms is a friendly, fully illustrated guide that teaches you how to apply common algorithms to practical problems face-to-face. You'll start with sorting and searching and, as you build up your skills in thinking algorithmically, you'll tackle more complex problems such as data compression and artificial intelligence.

fields.title: Domain-Driven Design
fields.description: This is not a book about specific technologies. It offers readers a systematic approach to domain-driven design, presenting an extensive set of modeling best practices, experience-based techniques, and fundamental principles that facilitate the development of software projects facing complex domains.

fields.title: Building Microservices
fields.description: As organizations shift from monolithic applications to smaller, self-contained microservices, software architecture is undergoing a revolution. In this second edition, Sam Newman provides a firm grounding in the concepts while diving deep into the latest practices for designing, integrating, testing, and deploying microservices.

fields.title: Computer Networking: A Top-Down Approach
fields.description: Motivates readers by introducing networking through the layered application perspective, providing a top-down, real-world context for learning internet protocols, network architectures, and transport layers.

fields.title: The Fellowship of the Ring
fields.description: One Ring to rule them all, One Ring to find them, One Ring to bring them all and in the darkness bind them. The first volume in J.R.R. Tolkien's epic masterpiece, recounting the gathering of the fellowship and the perilous quest toward Mordor to destroy the One Ring.

fields.title: The Hobbit
fields.description: Bilbo Baggins is a hobbit who enjoys a comfortable, unambitious life, rarely traveling any farther than his pantry or cellar. But his contentment is disturbed when the wizard Gandalf and a company of dwarves arrive on his doorstep one day to whisk him away on an adventure.

fields.title: A Game of Thrones
fields.description: Summers span decades. Winter can last a lifetime. And the struggle for the Iron Throne has begun. It will stretch from the south, where heat breeds plots, lusts and intrigues; to the vast and savage eastern lands; all the way to the frozen north, where an 800-foot wall of ice protects the kingdom.

fields.title: Ender's Game
fields.description: In order to develop a secure defense against a hostile alien race's next attack, government agencies breed child geniuses and train them as soldiers. A young boy, Andrew 'Ender' Wiggin, lives with his kind but distant parents, his sadistic brother Peter, and the person he loves more than anyone else, his sister Valentine.

fields.title: Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?
fields.description: By 2021, the World War has killed millions, driving entire species into extinction and sending mankind off-planet. Those who remained coveted any living creature, and for people who couldn't afford one, companies built incredibly realistic simulacra: androids. Rick Deckard is an officially sanctioned bounty hunter tasked with finding rogue Nexus-6 androids.

fields.title: Hyperion
fields.description: On the world called Hyperion, beyond the reach of galactic law, waits a creature called the Shrike. There are those who worship it. There are those who fear it. And there are those who have vowed to destroy it. On the eve of Armageddon, seven pilgrims set forth on a final voyage to Hyperion seeking the answers to the unsolved riddles of their lives.

fields.title: Snow Crash
fields.description: In reality, Hiro Protagonist delivers pizza for Uncle Enzo's CosoNostra Pizza Inc., but in the Metaverse he's a warrior prince. Plunging headlong into the enigma of a new computer virus that's striking down hackers everywhere, he races along the neon-lit streets on a search-and-destroy mission for the shadowy virtual villain.

fields.title: The Left Hand of Darkness
fields.description: A groundbreaking work of science fiction, The Left Hand of Darkness tells the story of a lone human emissary to Winter, an alien world whose inhabitants can choose and change their gender. His goal is to facilitate Winter's inclusion in a growing intergalactic civilization, but to do so he must bridge deep cultural divides.

fields.title: Fahrenheit 451
fields.description: Guy Montag is a fireman. His job is to destroy the most illegal of commodities, the printed book, along with the houses in which they are hidden. Montag never questions the destruction and ruin his actions produce, until he meets an eccentric young neighbor who introduces him to a past where people didn't live in fear.

fields.title: Solaris
fields.description: When Kris Kelvin arrives at the planet Solaris to study the ocean that covers its surface, he finds a mysterious, living sentient entity that probes the deepest memories and guilts of the human researchers stationed above it.

fields.title: I, Robot
fields.description: The Three Laws of Robotics: 1) A robot may not injure a human being or, through inaction, allow a human being to come to harm. 2) A robot must obey orders given it by human beings except where such orders would conflict with the First Law. 3) A robot must protect its own existence as long as such protection does not conflict with the First or Second Law.

fields.title: 2001: A Space Odyssey
fields.description: Written concurrently with Stanley Kubrick's cinematic masterpiece, Clarke's novel follows human evolution from ape-ancestors through the lunar discovery of a black monolith, and a voyage toward Saturn aboard the spaceship Discovery steered by the AI computer HAL 9000.

fields.title: Crime and Punishment
fields.description: Raskolnikov, an impoverished student living in the slums of Saint Petersburg, conceives of himself as an extraordinary young man freed from common moral constraints. He murders a pawnbroker and finds himself in an agonizing psychological duel with magistrate Porfiry Petrovich.

fields.title: The Brothers Karamazov
fields.description: Dostoevsky's final masterpiece is a passionate philosophical novel that enters deeply into the ethical debates of God, free will, morality, and family through the turbulent lives of three Russian brothers.

fields.title: War and Peace
fields.description: Tolstoy's panoramic masterwork portrays Napoleon's 1812 invasion of Russia and follows five aristocratic families through the horrors of battlefield combat, the splendors of Moscow society, and the search for personal spiritual redemption.

fields.title: Anna Karenina
fields.description: Acclaimed as the pinnacle of realist fiction, Anna Karenina unfolds against the backdrop of 19th-century imperial Russian society as the aristocratic Anna embarks on a tragic affair with Count Vronsky, while landowner Levin seeks quiet purpose.

fields.title: Wuthering Heights
fields.description: Lockwood, the new tenant of Thrushcross Grange on the bleak Yorkshire moors, is forced to seek shelter one night at Wuthering Heights, the home of his landlord Heathcliff. There he discovers the history of the tempestuous events that took place years before.

fields.title: Jane Eyre
fields.description: Orphaned as a child, Jane Eyre must overcome poverty and cruelty to forge her own independent path as a governess at Thornfield Hall, where she falls in love with the brooding, enigmatic Mr. Rochester only to discover a devastating secret.

fields.title: The Catcher in the Rye
fields.description: Holden Caulfield's iconic first-person account of the days following his expulsion from Pencey Prep school in Pennsylvania. Wandering through New York City, Holden observes the hypocrisy and phoniness of the adult world.

fields.title: Les Misérables
fields.description: The monumental epic of ex-convict Jean Valjean's struggle for redemption amidst the social turbulence of post-revolutionary France, pursued relentlessly by police inspector Javert, while young revolutionaries man the Paris barricades.

fields.title: The Picture of Dorian Gray
fields.description: Enthralled by his own exquisite portrait, youthful Dorian Gray makes a Faustian pledge that the painting will age and bear the marks of his sins while he maintains untouched physical youth, leading him down a spiral of aesthetic hedonism.

fields.title: Don Quixote
fields.description: Widely regarded as the first modern novel, Cervantes' masterpiece tells the hilarious and poignant story of an eccentric Spanish nobleman who becomes convinced he is a knight errant, setting out with his loyal squire Sancho Panza to right the world's wrongs.

fields.title: The Odyssey
fields.description: The epic tale of Odysseus' ten-year journey home to Ithaca after the fall of Troy, confronting mythical monsters, enchantresses, and vengeful gods, while his loyal wife Penelope fends off treacherous suitors.

fields.title: The Count of Monte Cristo
fields.description: Falsely accused of treason on the eve of his wedding, young sailor Edmond Dantès is imprisoned in the island fortress of the Château d'If. After escaping and finding a legendary buried treasure, he returns to Paris as the mysterious Count of Monte Cristo to exact meticulous revenge.

fields.title: Man's Search for Meaning
fields.description: Psychiatrist Viktor Frankl's memoir of his experiences in Auschwitz and Dachau, coupled with his development of logotherapy—the belief that human beings are fundamentally driven not by pleasure or power, but by the pursuit of meaning.

fields.title: Flow: The Psychology of Optimal Experience
fields.description: Legendary psychologist Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi's famous investigations of optimal experience reveal that what makes an experience genuinely satisfying is a state of consciousness called flow—intense absorption and joyful engagement where one's skills meet high challenges.

fields.title: Grit: The Power of Passion and Perseverance
fields.description: Pioneering psychologist Angela Duckworth shows that the secret to outstanding achievement is not innate talent, but a special blend of passion and persistence she calls 'grit.' Packed with insights from West Point cadets, National Spelling Bee finalists, and top educators.

fields.title: Quiet
fields.description: At least one-third of the people we know are introverts. They are the ones who prefer listening to speaking; who innovate and create but dislike self-promotion; who favor working on their own over working in teams. Susan Cain passionately argues that we dramatically undervalue introverts.

fields.title: Essentialism
fields.description: Have you ever found yourself stretched too thin? Essentialism isn't about how to get more things done; it's about how to get the right things done. It doesn't mean just doing less for the sake of less either. It is about making the wisest possible investment of your time and energy.

fields.title: Mindset: The New Psychology of Success
fields.description: World-renowned Stanford University psychologist Carol S. Dweck discovers that success in school, work, sports, the arts, and almost every area of human endeavor is influenced by how we think about our talents and abilities: having a fixed mindset versus a growth mindset.

fields.title: Influence: The Psychology of Persuasion
fields.description: Influence, the classic book on persuasion, explains the psychology of why people say 'yes'—and how to apply these understandings. Dr. Robert Cialdini is the seminal expert in the rapidly expanding field of influence and persuasion, identifying six universal principles.

fields.title: The Lean Startup
fields.description: Most startups fail. But many of those failures are preventable. The Lean Startup is a new approach being adopted across the globe, changing the way companies are built and new products are launched through validated learning, rapid experimentation, and the Build-Measure-Learn feedback loop.

fields.title: Good to Great
fields.description: Can a good company become a great company and, if so, how? Over five years, Jim Collins and his research team analyzed twenty-eight companies, discovering the key concepts that distinguish enduring greatness: Level 5 Leadership, the Hedgehog Concept, and the Flywheel Effect.

fields.title: Principles: Life and Work
fields.description: Ray Dalio, one of the world's most successful investors and entrepreneurs, shares the unconventional principles that he's developed, refined, and used over the past forty years to create unique results in both life and business at Bridgewater Associates.

fields.title: Freakonomics
fields.description: Which is more dangerous, a gun or a swimming pool? What do schoolteachers and sumo wrestlers have in common? Levitt and Dubner show that economics is, at root, the study of incentives—how people get what they want, or need, especially when other people want or need the same thing.

fields.title: Bad Blood
fields.description: The full inside story of the breathtaking rise and shocking collapse of Theranos, the multibillion-dollar biotech startup founded by Elizabeth Holmes, by the prize-winning journalist who first broke the story and pursued it to the end.

fields.title: Shoe Dog
fields.description: Bill Gates named Shoe Dog one of his five favorite books of 2016. In this candid and riveting memoir, Nike founder and board chairman Phil Knight shares the inside story of the company’s early days as an intrepid start-up and its evolution into one of the world's most iconic brands.

fields.title: The Selfish Gene
fields.description: Dawkins' brilliant reformulation of the theory of natural selection places the gene, rather than the organism or species, at center stage. He explains how selfish genes generate altruistic behavior, and coined the concept of the meme as a unit of cultural transmission.

fields.title: Gödel, Escher, Bach: An Eternal Golden Braid
fields.description: Winner of the Pulitzer Prize, Hofstadter's tour de force explores the nature of human consciousness and artificial intelligence through the self-referential mathematical theorems of Kurt Gödel, the optical illusions of M.C. Escher, and the contrapuntal music of J.S. Bach.

fields.title: The Elegant Universe
fields.description: Brian Greene, one of the world's leading string theorists, peels away the layers of mystery surrounding superstring theory to show that all matter and forces in the universe are composed of tiny, vibrating strings of energy operating in eleven dimensions.

fields.title: Six Easy Pieces
fields.description: Six Easy Pieces introduces the general reader to the most fundamental principles of physics—atoms, basic physics, the relation of physics to other sciences, energy, gravitation, and quantum behavior—distilled from Feynman's legendary Caltech lectures.

fields.title: Silent Spring
fields.description: First published in 1962, Silent Spring alerted a large audience to the environmental and human dangers of indiscriminate pesticide use, catalyzing the modern ecological movement and the founding of the EPA.

fields.title: What If?
fields.description: From the creator of the wildly popular webcomic xkcd, hilarious and informative answers to important questions you probably never thought to ask, using ballistics calculations, thermodynamics, and physics models.

fields.title: The Silk Roads
fields.description: An international bestseller and a major reassessment of world history, The Silk Roads shows how the heart of global civilization beat along the ancient arteries connecting East and West, where religions, trade goods, empires, and plagues shaped our destiny.

fields.title: The Lessons of History
fields.description: A concise survey of the culture and civilization of mankind, concluding the monumental Story of Civilization series. The Pulitzer Prize-winning historians compress five millennia of human triumphs and catastrophes into twelve illuminating essays.

fields.title: A People's History of the United States
fields.description: A People's History of the United States tells the story of America from the bottom up, centering the voices of Native Americans, enslaved laborers, immigrant factory workers, and women rather than presidents and generals.

fields.title: Justice: What's the Right Thing to Do?
fields.description: Based on his famous Harvard course, Sandel examines affirmative action, income inequality, military service, and individual rights through the moral lenses of utilitarianism, Immanuel Kant, John Locke, and Aristotle.

fields.title: Beyond Good and Evil
fields.description: Nietzsche dismantles conventional morality, philosophical dogmas, and religious systems, asserting the Will to Power and calling for free spirits to forge their own values beyond naive dualities of good and evil.

fields.title: The Republic
fields.description: Plato's central work features Socrates debating justice, the ideal state, the Allegory of the Cave, and the rule of Philosopher Kings, forming the cornerstone of Western political and philosophical thought.

fields.title: The Prince
fields.description: Machiavelli's notorious handbook for Renaissance rulers analyzes political power, fortune, and human nature with ruthless realism, asserting that effective leaders must know how to be feared as well as loved.

fields.title: Clean Architecture: A Craftsman's Guide to Software Structure and Design
fields.description: By applying universal rules of software architecture, you can dramatically improve developer productivity throughout the life of any software system. Now, building upon the success of his best-selling books Clean Code and The Clean Coder, legendary software craftsman Robert C. Martin reveals those rules and helps you apply them.

fields.title: The Phoenix Project: A Novel about IT, DevOps, and Helping Your Business Win
fields.description: Bill, an IT manager at Parts Unlimited, has been tasked with the impossible: rescue an over-budget, behind-schedule mission-critical project code-named Phoenix. With the company's survival at stake, Bill must revolutionize IT workflows, continuous integration, and operations using modern DevOps principles.

fields.title: Kubernetes: Up and Running: Dive into the Future of Infrastructure
fields.description: Legendary cloud native pioneers Brendan Burns, Joe Beda, and Kelsey Hightower explain how Kubernetes and container technology can help you achieve new levels of velocity, agility, reliability, and efficiency in distributed microservice deployments.

fields.title: Designing Distributed Systems: Patterns and Paradigms for Scalable, Reliable Services
fields.description: Without established patterns of distributed systems development, developers often end up reinventing the wheel. This practical book presents a collection of repeatable, generic patterns to make the development of reliable distributed systems far more approachable and efficient.

fields.title: System Design Interview: An Insider's Guide
fields.description: An indispensable guide to mastering large-scale distributed systems architecture, covering rate limiters, key-value stores, distributed message queues, web crawlers, real-time notification systems, and global chat backends.

fields.title: The DevOps Handbook: How to Create World-Class Agility, Reliability, and Security
fields.description: For decades, technology leaders have struggled to balance agility, reliability, and security. The DevOps Handbook provides concrete architectural roadmaps, automated CI/CD patterns, and organizational culture transformations to achieve continuous delivery.

fields.title: Chip War: The Fight for the World's Most Critical Technology
fields.description: Financial Times Business Book of the Year. An illuminating history of how microchips became the new oil—the scarce resource modern civilization depends on—and the fierce geopolitical battle to control semiconductor manufacturing.

fields.title: The Art of Computer Programming, Volume 1: Fundamental Algorithms
fields.description: The bible of computer science. Professor Donald Knuth's monumental masterwork introduces fundamental mathematical preliminaries, algorithmic notation, data structures, trees, dynamic storage allocation, and information manipulation.

fields.title: Compilers: Principles, Techniques, and Tools
fields.description: Known affectionately to software engineers worldwide as the Dragon Book, this definitive text covers lexical analysis, syntax-directed translation, intermediate code generation, runtime environments, and modern optimization techniques.

fields.title: Operating Systems: Three Easy Pieces
fields.description: A beloved, crystal-clear textbook covering the foundational pillars of modern operating systems: CPU and memory virtualization, multi-threaded concurrency synchronization, and durable file system persistence.

fields.title: Computer Systems: A Programmer's Perspective
fields.description: By explaining how assembly code executes on hardware, how linkers resolve references, how caches optimize latency, and how virtual memory isolates processes, CS:APP bridges the gap between hardware architecture and high-performance software.

fields.title: Introduction to the Theory of Computation
fields.description: The most celebrated theoretical computer science text. Michael Sipser presents automata theory, regular expressions, context-free grammars, Turing machines, computability, and NP-completeness with unmatched pedagogical elegance.

fields.title: Database System Concepts
fields.description: The premier academic standard on relational database engines, indexing structures (B+ trees, LSM trees), SQL query optimization, ACID concurrency control, write-ahead logging, and distributed transactions.

fields.title: The Mythical Man-Month: Essays on Software Engineering
fields.description: Few books on software project management have been as influential and enduring. Fred Brooks reveals timeless software truths, including Brooks's Law: "Adding manpower to a late software project makes it later."

fields.title: Deep Learning with Python
fields.description: Written by Keras creator François Chollet, this book introduces the field of deep learning using Python and the powerful Keras and TensorFlow frameworks. It features intuitive explanations and zero mathematical obfuscation.

fields.title: Project Hail Mary
fields.description: Ryland Grace is the sole survivor on a desperate, last-chance mission to save humanity from an interstellar extinction event. He just has to figure out who he is, remember his scientific training, and collaborate with an unexpected ally.

fields.title: The Martian
fields.description: Six days ago, astronaut Mark Watney became one of the first people to walk on Mars. Now, he is stranded alone on the hostile Martian surface after a dust storm forces his crew to evacuate. Armed only with his ingenuity and engineering skills, he must survive.

fields.title: Rendezvous with Rama
fields.description: A massive cylindrical alien vessel enters the solar system in the twenty-second century. A team of human astronauts is dispatched to explore the enigmatic, spinning world within world, uncovering awe-inspiring extraterrestrial artifacts.

fields.title: Contact
fields.description: Astronomer Ellie Arroway discovers the first confirmed extraterrestrial transmission from the Vega system, carrying plans for a mysterious machine that will carry a human voyager across the fabric of spacetime.

fields.title: Children of Time
fields.description: Arthur C. Clarke Award Winner. A terraformed world seeded with an evolutionary virus fosters an advanced civilization of sentient arachnids, whose fate converges with the remnants of humanity fleeing a ruined Earth on an ark ship.

fields.title: The Forever War
fields.description: Private William Mandella is drafted into an interstellar war against an elusive alien race. But because of relativistic time dilation, every tour of duty takes months for him, while centuries pass on Earth.

fields.title: Station Eleven
fields.description: National Book Award Finalist. In a post-pandemic North America where civilization has collapsed, a nomadic troupe of actors and musicians called The Traveling Symphony travels between settlements performing Shakespeare and music.

fields.title: Childhood's End
fields.description: Giant alien spaceships suddenly appear over Earth's major cities. Known as the Overlords, these peaceful beings end war, poverty, and disease—yet refuse to show themselves, leading humanity toward a transcendent and startling destiny.

fields.title: The Old Man and the Sea
fields.description: Hemingway's immortal masterpiece of Santiago, an aging Cuban fisherman who struggles alone in the Gulf Stream against a giant marlin. An unforgettable testament to human courage, resilience, and endurance.

fields.title: The Road
fields.description: A father and his young son walk alone through burned America. Nothing moves in the ravaged landscape save the ash on the wind. They have nothing; just a pistol to defend themselves, the clothes they are wearing, and each other.

fields.title: The Stranger
fields.description: Through the story of an ordinary, detached man unwittingly drawn into a senseless murder on an Algerian beach, Camus explores what he termed "the nakedness of man faced with the absurd."

fields.title: Catch-22
fields.description: Set in Italy during World War II, this hilarious and profound satirical masterpiece chronicles the heroic struggles of Bombardier Yossarian to survive the bureaucratic lunacy of military command.

fields.title: Slaughterhouse-Five
fields.description: Billy Pilgrim has come unstuck in time. Centered around the firebombing of Dresden, Vonnegut's anti-war classic combines biting dark humor, science fiction, and profound moral reflection.

fields.title: Things Fall Apart
fields.description: Achebe's seminal masterpiece portrays the tragic fall of Okonkwo, an Igbo warrior and leader in Nigeria, as European colonial administration and missionaries disrupt traditional society.

fields.title: The Master and Margarita
fields.description: A dazzling literary masterpiece of twentieth-century Russian literature. The devil, in the guise of Professor Woland, arrives in 1930s Moscow accompanied by a talking black cat with a penchant for vodka and chess.

fields.title: Blindness
fields.description: A city is hit by an epidemic of "white blindness" that spares only one woman. A searing allegory of human resilience, civilization's fragility, and moral fortitude.

fields.title: SPQR: A History of Ancient Rome
fields.description: World-renowned Cambridge classicist Mary Beard explores how Rome grew from an obscure village into an undisputed global superpower, examining Roman democracy, slavery, warfare, citizenship, and power dynamics.

fields.title: Team of Rivals: The Political Genius of Abraham Lincoln
fields.description: Winner of the Lincoln Prize. A monumental biography focusing on Lincoln's brilliant political mastery in appointing his fiercest political rivals into his cabinet to preserve the American Union during the Civil War.

fields.title: The Wright Brothers
fields.description: Two-time Pulitzer Prize winner David McCullough tells the dramatic, inspiring story of Wilbur and Orville Wright, two courageous bicycle mechanics from Ohio who solved the mystery of powered human flight.

fields.title: Churchill: A Life
fields.description: The definitive single-volume biography by Sir Winston Churchill's official biographer. Draws from private diaries, top-secret telegrams, and state archives to recount his leadership during World War II.

fields.title: Genghis Khan and the Making of the Modern World
fields.description: An astonishing revisionist history showing how the Mongol empire under Genghis Khan introduced paper currency, religious tolerance, diplomatic immunity, and unified global trade routes across Eurasia.

fields.title: Alexander Hamilton
fields.description: The New York Times bestseller that inspired the smash hit musical. Ron Chernow presents the gripping biography of an illegitimate Caribbean orphan who became George Washington's right hand and the architect of American capitalism.

fields.title: The Crusades: The Authoritative History of the War for the Holy Land
fields.description: A monumental, balanced, and gripping history of the centuries-long conflict between Christians and Muslims for control of Jerusalem and the Near East, told through both Western and Islamic contemporary sources.

fields.title: Postwar: A History of Europe Since 1945
fields.description: Pulitzer Prize Finalist. An unparalleled, sweeping account of how Europe recovered from the catastrophic destruction of World War II to rebuild its democratic institutions, welfare states, and supranational unity.

fields.title: Nicomachean Ethics
fields.description: Aristotle explores eudaimonia (human flourishing) and the nature of moral virtue, defining virtue as the golden mean between excess and deficiency in human actions and emotions.

fields.title: Letters from a Stoic
fields.description: Seneca offers practical, timeless advice on overcoming fear, bearing adversity with dignity, valuing true friendship, mastering time, and finding tranquility amidst imperial chaos.

fields.title: Critique of Pure Reason
fields.description: Kant synthesizes rationalism and empiricism, establishing synthetic a priori judgments and investigating the conditions of possible experience through space, time, and transcendental categories.

fields.title: Thus Spoke Zarathustra
fields.description: Nietzsche's philosophical poem introducing the Übermensch, the Will to Power, and the Eternal Recurrence through the visionary prophet Zarathustra descending from his mountain retreat.

fields.title: Discourse on Method and Meditations on First Philosophy
fields.description: Descartes lays down radical skepticism and arrives at the indubitable foundation of all knowledge: Cogito, ergo sum ("I think, therefore I am"), establishing Cartesian dualism.

fields.title: The Myth of Sisyphus
fields.description: Camus confronts the ultimate philosophical question: does the absurdity of existence require suicide? His defiant conclusion: one must imagine Sisyphus happy as he pushes his rock up the mountain.

fields.title: Existentialism Is a Humanism
fields.description: Sartre's clearest and most accessible defense of existentialist ethics: existence precedes essence, meaning humans are condemned to be free and must actively define their own values.

fields.title: Predictably Irrational: The Hidden Forces That Shape Our Decisions
fields.description: MIT behavioral economist Dan Ariely refutes the common assumption that we behave in fundamentally rational ways. Through entertaining experiments, he shows systematic errors in our thinking.

fields.title: The Power of Habit: Why We Do What We Do in Life and Business
fields.description: Award-winning New York Times reporter Charles Duhigg explains the neurological habit loop (cue, routine, reward) and reveals how individuals and organizations can transform their lives by altering keystone habits.

fields.title: Blink: The Power of Thinking Without Thinking
fields.description: An examination of the instant judgments we make in the blink of an eye—how expert "thin-slicing" works, why snap decisions can be astonishingly accurate, and when subconscious biases mislead us.

fields.title: Drive: The Surprising Truth About What Motivates Us
fields.description: Forget carrots and sticks. Daniel Pink exposes the mismatch between what science knows and what business does, proving that high performance is driven by autonomy, mastery, and purpose.

fields.title: The Man Who Mistook His Wife for a Hat
fields.description: Neurologist Oliver Sacks recounts fascinating, compassionate clinical case studies of patients navigating profound neurological disorders, agnosias, phantom limbs, and Tourette's syndrome.

fields.title: Behave: The Biology of Humans at Our Best and Worst
fields.description: Stanford neurobiologist Robert Sapolsky delivers a monumental investigation into why humans act the way they do, tracing neurochemical impulses seconds before action back to evolutionary pressures over millennia.

fields.title: Stumbling on Happiness
fields.description: Harvard psychologist Daniel Gilbert reveals why human imagination struggles to accurately forecast what will make us happy in the future, using witty analogies and cutting-edge cognitive experiments.

fields.title: The Innovator's Dilemma: When New Technologies Cause Great Firms to Fail
fields.description: One of the most influential business books ever written. Harvard professor Clayton Christensen outlines disruptive innovation and why market-leading companies often fail precisely by doing everything right.

fields.title: Thinking in Bets: Making Smarter Decisions When You Don't Have All the Facts
fields.description: World Series of Poker champion turned business consultant Annie Duke shows how to decouple decision quality from outcomes, combat cognitive biases, and make smarter strategic bets under deep uncertainty.

fields.title: The Hard Thing About Hard Things: Building a Business When There Are No Easy Answers
fields.description: Andreessen Horowitz co-founder Ben Horowitz shares brutal, unvarnished wisdom on managing startups through crises, firing friends, poaching executives, and leading when catastrophe strikes.

fields.title: Capital in the Twenty-First Century
fields.description: An international sensation. French economist Thomas Piketty analyzes historic wealth distribution data across three centuries, showing that whenever return on capital exceeds economic growth (r > g), inequality widens.

fields.title: Liar's Poker: Rising Through the Wreckage on Wall Street
fields.description: Michael Lewis's riotous insider tell-all of Salomon Brothers trading desks during the wild 1980s bond market boom, capturing greed, ambition, and financial engineering in vivid detail.

fields.title: Built to Last: Successful Habits of Visionary Companies
fields.description: Drawing on a six-year research project at Stanford Business School, Collins and Porras examine eighteen visionary companies to discover what distinguishes enduringly great institutions from their competitors.

fields.title: Rework
fields.description: From the creators of Basecamp, Rework discards traditional corporate dogma. It shows that you need less than you think—less staff, fewer meetings, less planning—to build a wildly profitable and resilient business.

fields.title: The Gene: An Intimate History
fields.description: Pulitzer Prize winner Siddhartha Mukherjee traces the fascinating history of the gene from Aristotle to Mendel, Darwin, Watson and Crick, up to modern CRISPR gene-editing technologies.

fields.title: The Emperor of All Maladies: A Biography of Cancer
fields.description: Winner of the Pulitzer Prize. A magnificent "biography" of cancer—from its earliest recorded appearances in ancient Egyptian scrolls to the heroic twentieth-century battles to cure it.

fields.title: Seven Brief Lessons on Physics
fields.description: A lean, poetic introduction to modern physics covering general relativity, quantum mechanics, the architecture of the cosmos, elementary particles, quantum gravity, black holes, and time.

fields.title: Chaos: Making a New Science
fields.description: National Book Award Finalist. James Gleick recounts the discovery of chaos theory—from the butterfly effect to fractals and strange attractors—revealing universal order hidden in turbulent systems.

fields.title: Fermat's Enigma: The Epic Quest to Solve the World's Greatest Mathematical Problem
fields.description: The thrilling story of Andrew Wiles's seven-year secret struggle to prove Fermat's Last Theorem, solving a mathematical riddle that had puzzled the world's greatest minds for over 350 years.

fields.title: The Character of Physical Law
fields.description: Nobel laureate Richard Feynman delivers seven legendary lectures on gravitation, mathematics, conservation principles, symmetry, the arrow of time, and quantum mechanics with unmatched clarity.

fields.title: The Fabric of the Cosmos: Space, Time, and the Texture of Reality
fields.description: Theoretical physicist Brian Greene takes readers on an exhilarating journey through the fundamental structure of reality, from Newton's absolute space to Einstein's warped spacetime, quantum entanglement, and 11-dimensional string theory.
